Zelechow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Żelechów, Poland

Demolished. Jews are recorded in Żelechów from the 16th century; by 1921, 4,016 Jews lived there, most murdered at Treblinka in 1942. This original cemetery, likely established in the first half of the 18th century, stood beside the town synagogue and is first documented in a 1750 episcopal decree restricting Jewish burial practices. Tzadik Aron Hopstein was buried here in 1776 beneath an ohel. Around 1801-1802, sanitation concerns prompted local authorities to order the community to stop using this site and establish a new cemetery outside town limits. This original site was presumably destroyed during WWII; the synagogue was demolished after 1945 and the area became a park, formalized with a memorial stone around 2011.
